plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers directly from the ground in autumn, without any leaves present. The leaves appear the following spring and die back by summer. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to damp meadows in Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used to treat gout and used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling. Its leafless autumn flowers earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, hairy-stemmed perennial that forms large clumps covered in daisy-like flowers with golden-yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators and thrives in meadows, roadsides and prairies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to Alabama; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: New England asters are a key stopover food source for migrating monarch butterflies, which refuel on their nectar during their journey to Mexico in September.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose bright red, spidery flowers with long curved stamens emerge on leafless stalks in early autumn. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering and persist through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to China, Korea and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan, these flowers bloom around the autumn equinox (Higanbana) and are traditionally planted along rice paddies and graves; their toxic bulbs deter rodents and moles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, featuring a bowl of showy pinkish bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny true flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November), peaking around September
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii and California
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change shape, reflecting the group's great diversity.
